binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω, equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure μ instance.
An exponent p in the extended nonnegative reals ENNReal = [0, ∞].
A real-valued function X : Ω → ℝ.
conclusions: The representative-membership predicate stored in LocalDef003 μ p holds for X if and only if eLpNorm X p μ < ∞; since that stored predicate is MemLp X p μ, this says MemLp X p μ ↔ eLpNorm X p μ < ∞.
The quotient additive subgroup stored in LocalDef003 μ p is equal to MeasureTheory.Lp Real p μ, the standard Lp subgroup of real-valued functions modulo μ-almost-everywhere equality.
mathematical_definitions: AEStronglyMeasurable X μ means that X is μ-almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function.
MemLp X p μ means AEStronglyMeasurable X μ ∧ eLpNorm X p μ < ∞.
eLpNorm uses 0 at p = 0, the essential-supremum norm at p = ∞, and eLpNorm' with exponent p.toReal otherwise.
AEEqFun Ω Real μ consists of real-valued functions modulo μ-almost-everywhere equality.
MeasureTheory.Lp Real p μ is the additive subgroup of AEEqFun Ω Real μ whose elements have eLpNorm below ∞.
LocalDef003 μ p is a concrete package whose representative norm is eLpNorm, whose representative-membership predicate is MemLp, and whose quotient field is MeasureTheory.Lp Real p μ.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable type Ω, every probability measure μ on Ω, every extended-nonnegative exponent p other than 0, and every real-valued μ-almost-everywhere strongly measurable function X, two statements hold: X satisfies the representative-membership predicate in the concrete package LocalDef003 μ p exactly when its extended Lp seminorm is finite, and the quotient subgroup in that package is exactly the standard real-valued Lp subgroup. After expanding the package and MemLp, the first statement is (AEStronglyMeasurable X μ ∧ eLpNorm X p μ < ∞) ↔ eLpNorm X p μ < ∞ under the supplied measurability hypothesis, while the second is the reflexive equality MeasureTheory.Lp Real p μ = MeasureTheory.Lp Real p μ.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure is restricted to probability measures even though the displayed definitions and conclusions are formulated for arbitrary measures and the probability-measure instance does not otherwise occur in them.
The exponent restriction is only p ≠ 0. Thus p = ∞ is included, as are finite exponents below 1; no assumption 1 ≤ p < ∞ is encoded.
The p ≠ 0 hypothesis is not needed for the displayed definitional MemLp equivalence or for the quotient-field equality; it unnecessarily removes the p = 0 case from the theorem's applicability.

The function is restricted by an explicit almost-everywhere strong-measurability hypothesis. This makes the MemLp biconditional collapse to finiteness of eLpNorm; the theorem does not characterize arbitrary nonmeasurable representatives.
The second conjunct is independent of X and its measurability hypothesis and is definitionally true from the construction of LocalDef003.
The target identifies an additive subgroup of almost-everywhere equivalence classes; it does not assert normed-space completeness, a metric or norm equality, or any analytic inequality for Lp.

There is no evident impossible-premise vacuity: standard probability spaces and nonzero ENNReal exponents exist, but quantification is conditional on the supplied probability-measure and measurability instances.
ambiguities: The packet gives only the type of IsProbabilityMeasure, not its field-level definition; its exact effect is nevertheless clear at the target level as a probability-measure typeclass restriction on μ.

The internal definitions of eLpNormEssSup and eLpNorm' are outside the one-level dependency boundary, so the packet determines the exponent case split but not their expanded integral or essential-supremum formulas.
Several structure proof bodies are elided as ⋯, but their complete types are shown and those proof terms do not affect the proposition translated here.
